The same principle applies to other sections of the PBRER in which the MAH summarises new, clinically important efficacy/effectiveness information that became available during the interval covered by the PBRER.

f.title: Cross-reference earlier sections for clinical trial efficacy/effectiveness information instead of duplicating it in Section 17.2
f.statement: If new clinically important efficacy/effectiveness information from clinical trials has been included in previous sections of the PBRER (e.g. Sections 7, 9.1 or 13), the MAH should include cross-references to the relevant section(s) rather than duplicating it; Section 17.2 is therefore likely to focus on new information on efficacy/effectiveness under conditions of actual use.

f.title: Summarise efficacy/effectiveness information on unapproved indications only if it may affect the approved-indication benefit-risk
f.statement: Whether information is "relevant" is a matter of judgement. The MAH should consider whether new efficacy/effectiveness information relating to an unapproved indication may have an impact on the benefit-risk profile for the approved indication(s) and, if so, should summarise the new information accordingly.

f.statement: The Guideline does not exclude a benefit-risk assessment within the context of a local label, which would most likely occur at the request of a specific regulatory authority for a specific product.
